text: . Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a two-day visit to Karnataka and Gujarat beginning tomorrow. He will participate in the Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram, the residential headquarters campus of Swami Vivekananda Yoga Anusandhana Samsthana (S-VYASA), tomorrow morning. In the afternoon, the Prime Minister will flag off and undertake a metro ride from Tavarekere to IIM Bangalore metro station. After this, Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate, and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 15,600 crore rupees in Bengaluru.On the same day, the Prime Minister will travel to Mysuru, where he will participate in a tree plantation programme at Bharat Vann. In the evening, he will inaugurate COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium. On Saturday, the Prime Minister will perform Darshan and Pooja at Ambaji temple in Banaskantha, Gujarat. Ambaji Temple is one of the 51 revered Shakti Peethas.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. Indian boxers Gunjan and Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei have stormed into the finals of the Summer Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, keeping India’s hopes of two gold medals alive.Gunjan beat Great Britain’s Lily Bassett 4-1 in the women’s 48-kilogram semifinal yesterday. She will now face Algeria’s Bouthaina Bensalah in the final.Meetei was actually the first Indian boxer to reach the finals at these Youth Olympics. He got to the men’s 50-kilogram final after winning 5-0 against Izzon Jeffrey Galea Arevalo from Colombia in the semifinal bout.Meetei will face Kristian Jubani from Ireland for the gold.  So far, India have won nine medals at the Games, including three silver and six bronze in wrestling, boxing, and swimming. The Youth Olympics 2026 ends on the 13th of this month.

. Niraj Kumar today won the bronze medal in the men’s 50m rifle three-positions event at the World Shooting Championships in Doha. Niraj has also secured a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.This marks India’s second Olympic quota from the championships. Previously, Jaypal Malviya had secured the first quota by winning a silver medal in the men’s 10m air pistol event.

. India today defeated Maldives 1-0 in SAFF Championship Group B match at the National Stadium in Dhaka. Suhail Ahmad Bhat scored the match’s lone goal from the penalty spot in the 38th minute. With this the Blue Tigers entered the semi-finals.It was India’s second and final group match of the South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) Championships.India beat Pakistan 3-2 in their opening Group B match on 5th of this month.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange colour warning for heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms over Jammu and Kashmir today.Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days. Similar weather conditions are expected over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for the day. IMD has advised fishermen to avoid venturing into the Andaman Sea till the 16th of this month. Meanwhile, air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the Very Poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 321 as of 7 AM today.

. Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has resigned, raising the prospect of a political rift between President Prabowo Subianto and former President Joko Widodo. Mr. Gibran submitted his resignation to President Prabowo amid mounting scrutiny over his education credentials following court rulings that found his documents did not meet election requirements.Mr. Gibran tendered his resignation yesterday, while two parliamentary sources said he would submit a formal letter to the upper house today. The development follows a petition by about 120 lawmakers seeking Mr. Gibran’s impeachment over his eligibility to serve as vice president. Now the Indonesian upper house must declare the position vacant and hold an election for a replacement within 60 days, according to senior law minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra.The resignation also threatens to strain the political alliance between President Prabowo and former President Widodo, potentially deepening uncertainty in Southeast Asia’s largest economy.

. In the Under-19 Asia Cup Cricket, India secured a place in the semi-finals after defeating the United Arab Emirates by 70 runs at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman today.Put into bat first, India set a target of 310 runs and then restricted the UAE to 239 runs in 50 overs. India had scored 309 losing 7 wickets in 50 overs.India’s Aryavir Sehwag was named Player of the Match for his impressive knock of 160 off 168 balls. India will now take on Afghanistan in the semi-final on Thursday.

. Ladghar and Guhagar beaches in Ratnagiri district and Shrivardhan beach in Raigad district of Maharashtra have received the prestigious International ‘Blue Flag’ award for the 2026-27 season, marking the first time Maharashtra has secured international recognition under the programme.The beaches have met international standards for environmental conservation, cleanliness, water quality, biodiversity protection, tourist safety, infrastructure and sustainable tourism management. The achievement reflects coordinated efforts by the State Government’s Environment and Climate Change Department and Tourism Department, district administrations, local bodies and communities.The Blue Flag season for the three beaches will commence on 15th November 2026. The official flags are being brought from the Netherlands, following which a flag-hoisting ceremony will be organised.Congratulating the achievement, Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde said the recognition would enhance Maharashtra’s identity on the global tourism map and boost local employment and economic activity. She said the State Government, under the guidance of Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, would continue efforts to develop other eligible beaches to international standards and promote sustainable tourism.

. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) Women’s Selection Committee has announced squads for the upcoming all-format tour of South Africa in December. Smriti Mandhana is set to lead the side across all three formats.India will play one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is during the tour, which will begin with the Test match in Gqeberha on 9th December. The ODI series will start on 16th December in Paarl, followed by the second match in Cape Town on 19th December and the third in Bloemfontein on 22nd December. The three-match T20I series will begin on December 26 in Benoni. The second and third matches are scheduled to be played in Potchefstroom.Deepti Sharma has been named vice-captain of the Test and ODI squads, while Shafali Verma will serve as vice-captain in the T20I format. The Test squad features 15 players, including Harmanpreet Kaur, Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh, Yastika Bhatia, Sneh Rana and Kranti Gaud. The ODI squad also comprises 15 players, with Vaishnavi Sharma included in place of Sneh Rana from the Test squad. The T20I squad has 17 players, with Shafali Verma as vice-captain. Niki Prasad, G. Kamalini, Anushka Sharma, Prema Rawat, Amanjot Kaur, Renuka Singh Thakur and Arundhati Reddy are also part of the squad.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Anuj Shrivatri on becoming India’s 100th Chess Grandmaster, describing the achievement as a proud moment for the country. In a message on social media, the Prime Minister said India has reached a century in chess. He said the achievement reflects the immense talent, dedication and hard work of Indian chess players, as well as the growing popularity of the game among young people.The Prime Minister expressed hope that the milestone would inspire more youngsters to take up chess and strive for excellence. Anuj Shrivatri, who hails from Madhya Pradesh, achieved the milestone after winning the seventh ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship in the Philippines on Sunday. With this achievement, India has reached the landmark of 100 Grandmasters. Chess legend Viswanathan Anand became the country’s first Grandmaster in 1988.India has added five Grandmasters between July and November this year. Before Anuj Shrivatri, Ethan Vaz, Harshvardhan G B, S Ashwath and V Rathnavel had earned the prestigious title. India is also home to reigning World Chess Champion D. Gukesh, who is set to defend his world title later this month.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. The government today launched the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards to recognise outstanding startups across the country. The awards recognise not just commercial success but also social impact, sustainability, and scalability. Launching the awards in New Delhi today, DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh said that startups can apply under 20 sectoral categories. He said that in addition, there are three special categories for women, students, and the North Eastern region. He added that the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade is at the forefront of driving reforms to promote startups. Mr Singh also emphasised the need for more private initiative to bring more startups in the country. He expressed hope that the awards would further boost the startup ecosystem in the country. The Secretary highlighted that the award covers a wide range of domains including agriculture, fintech, aerospace, health, education, and accessibility, among others. The applications for the award will remain open until 20 November this year.In line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the goal of a five-trillion-dollar economy, Startup India supports startups through initiatives such as startup recognition, tax exemptions, regulatory ease, funding access, and capacity building. Launched in 2016, Startup India has transformed India’s entrepreneurial landscape, fostering innovation and empowering youth, women, students, and first-time founders, particularly from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Over two lakh 25 thousand startups have been recognised by DPIIT so far.

. In Europe, over 6,300 schools across Italy and over 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats, leading to evacuations. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said initial checks found no evidence of a concrete threat. She described the messages as an apparent attempt to spread panic.In Scotland, Education Secretary Mairi McAllan said there was no risk to the public. Police assessed the warnings as hoaxes and launched investigations to trace their source.Northern Ireland authorities advised schools to remain open unless police told them otherwise. Italy’s Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara also said the incidents were likely a cyberattack, not a genuine security threat.The incidents caused alarm among parents and school staff, but authorities said investigations are continuing.European officials suspect Russia of orchestrating disruptions in countries supporting Ukraine, an allegation Moscow denies.Iran is also under suspicion after France accused it of a cyberattack that disabled refrigerators in hundreds of supermarkets. Tehran has also rejected the allegations as baseless and hostile.

. India and South Africa reviewed the entire gamut of the Strategic Partnership and explored avenues for further deepening bilateral cooperation across diverse sectors. The 12th round of Foreign Office Consultations between the two countries was co-chaired by Joint Secretary (East and South Africa) in Ministry of External Affairs, Janesh Kain, and Ambassador David Malcomson, Acting DDG of South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation.

. Indian American astronaut and retired Navy Captain Sunita Williams was honoured as Grand Marshal of New York’s 107th annual Veterans Day Parade, leading about 20,000 participants along Manhattan’s Fifth Avenue yesterday. She called the honour incredible, saying her Navy service shaped her and prepared her for future challenges. Williams completed three space missions, spending 608 days in space and setting a record for women with nine spacewalks totalling 62 hours. She made headlines in 2024 when an eight-day mission to the International Space Station aboard Boeing’s Starliner extended to nine months because of technical problems. She and fellow astronaut Butch Wilmore eventually returned to Earth aboard a SpaceX Crew-9 mission.

Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. In Pakistan, 11 police personnel and 18 attackers were killed in an ambush in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province yesterday. Police said the team was returning from an operation against illegal gold mining in Kohat district when attackers opened fire from nearby hilltops in the Darbokach Jalandhar Banda area. The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police said the personnel were conducting a joint operation with the local civil administration.Police personnel fought the attackers with great bravery and courage, as a result of which 18 attackers were killed.Deputy Superintendent of Police Haider Zaman and Sub-Inspector Mukhtiar were among those killed. Five police vehicles were also set ablaze.An emergency was declared at the District Headquarters Teaching Hospital. Provincial Governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the attack, describing it as a nexus between criminal elements and terrorists.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading three and a half per cent down at 94 US dollars and 92 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 2.8 per cent lower at 87 US dollars and seven cents per barrel, when reports last came in.
